title: multi-sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics and parity bump v1.211.0
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: bring Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to parity for auth and retry behavior, standardize streaming ergonomics, and publish a coordinated patch release v1.211.0. This PR unifies token refresh behavior, simplifies retry configuration surface, and stabilizes streaming client APIs so embedders get the same developer ergonomics across languages. Context: multiple downstream teams reported subtle differences in auth refresh timing and streaming backpressure semantics (see ENG-4201). This change reduces customer support load and avoids surprising 401 spikes during token rotations. Changes (high level): - Auth: centralized refresh logic and unified token cache semantics. Python: introduced AuthManager with background refresh jitter and singleflight refresh suppression. TS: exported same AuthManager surface in src/auth.ts and improved typed credentials helper. Go: consolidated token provider interface and added singleflight dedupe for refreshes. - Retries: standardized default retryable errors and backoff settings across SDKs; added explicit RetryPolicy object that is configurably composable. - Streaming APIs: simplified client stream iteration patterns, introduced unified on_message/on_error/on_close hooks across languages, and improved automatic reconnect/backoff for transient EOFs. - Ergonomics: removed duplicate configuration keys, added clearer defaults, and improved documentation and type hints across SDKs. - Parity bump: updated package.json/go.mod/pyproject versions and changelogs for coordinated release. Migration notes: existing apps should continue to work with old config keys (compat layer preserved for two minor releases); recommended to switch to the new RetryPolicy and AuthManager for improved reliability. Backwards compatibility: no breaking changes expected; a migration note is included in the changelog and release notes. Testing: added unit and integration tests across all three SDKs, end-to-end smoke against the hosted API in CI, and a short canary rollout for Dedicated customers. Rollout: staged release with feature flags for streaming reconnect, monitor metrics (401-rate, token-refresh-latency, stream-reconnects) via Redwood Console dashboards. Checklist: - [x] Implement language-specific changes - [x] Add unit/integration tests - [x] Update docs & changelogs - [x] Bump versions and publish release notes - [x] Get approvals from SDK leads and infra reviewers Related: ENG-4201, PM-332, SUP-998.

review_comments: Miguel Rivera: Nice to see the singleflight dedupe. One concern: the default refresh threshold is 60s which might be too aggressive for short-lived tokens. Can we make that configurable and add a metrics tag?
Asha Patel: Agreed, made threshold configurable via AuthManager.refresh_window and added token_refresh.window tag to metrics. Updated tests to cover both default and custom windows.
Sofia Chen: TypeScript types look good. Suggest adding a small example in README to show streaming reconnect usage (on_message/on_error/on_close).
Asha Patel: Added example in examples/stream-reconnect/README.md and linked it from docs/sdks/streaming.md.
Liam O'Connor: Integration test flaked once in CI (stream reconnect test). Reran and passed. Add retry for flaky test in CI so we don't block future runs.
Asha Patel: Added `retry: 2` to the flaky test matrix and filed follow-up ENG-4210 to fully root cause intermittent EOFs.
